questions.question: Developers and operations staff share some permissions. An administrator wants a single "Engineering" group that contains both the Developers and Operations groups. What happens?
options: It works; groups can be nested one level
It fails; groups can contain users only
It works only for inline policies
It works if both groups are in one Region
questions.explanation: IAM groups contain users only, so nesting fails; there is no one-level nesting, inline policies do not change this, and IAM is global so Regions are irrelevant.

questions.question: Fred belongs to no group but needs read access to one bucket. What is the most direct way to grant it?
options: Add Fred to the root account
Attach an inline policy to Fred
Create a group containing only the bucket
questions.explanation: An inline policy grants permissions to a single user; root access and credential sharing break least privilege, and groups cannot contain resources.

questions.question: An auditor needs only to list and describe EC2 instances. Which policy best applies least privilege?
questions.explanation: Describe actions grant exactly the read access needed; ec2:* and * add write permissions, and Deny would block the requirement.

questions.question: A new company opens its first AWS account. What should be done with the root account after initial setup?
options: Use it for daily tasks with a strong password
Avoid using it and create IAM users instead
questions.explanation: Root should not be used or shared; create IAM users for daily work. Sharing or daily use exposes full access, and the root account cannot simply be deleted while the account exists.

questions.question: Alice is in the Developers group and the Audit group. Which permissions does she receive?
options: Only the first group she was added to
None until a single group is chosen
questions.explanation: Users inherit the policies of every group they belong to; there is no first-group or single-group rule.

questions.question: In a policy statement, which element specifies the API calls being allowed or denied?
questions.explanation: Action lists the API calls; Resource is the target, Principal the identity, and Sid only an optional statement identifier.

questions.question: Which statement about IAM policies is correct?
options: Effect can be Allow or Deny
Condition is required in every statement
questions.explanation: Effect takes Allow or Deny; policies are JSON, Version should always be "2012-10-17", and Condition is optional.

questions.question: Compare a group policy with an inline policy. Which is true?
options: A group policy applies to every member; an inline policy to one user
An inline policy applies to every group
questions.explanation: Group policies apply to all members while inline policies attach to one user; inline policies are not group-wide, there is no override ranking between them, and they can Allow or Deny.
